title: Partial recursive functions: search and divergence

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 9 (§1.2, partial functions); 33–35 (§2.5, strict partial operations, minimization and recursive functions; version 2007-01-09)

summary: Allow searches to run without a bound, keeping track of exactly when an output exists and when an earlier computation blocks the search.
abstract: To find a natural number with a given property, we can test candidates in order. When a candidate works, the search stops; when none works, it can continue forever. There is another possibility: testing one candidate may itself never finish, preventing the search from reaching a later successful candidate. A partial function records the outputs that exist and leaves other inputs undefined. Starting with primitive recursion, we add sequential unbounded search and prove exactly when it returns the least successful candidate. Searches that are guaranteed to find a witness give total recursive functions, while the same construction also describes procedures that finish only on some inputs.
